text: Here is a mistake the June 2023 examiners reported. Our framing: explain why glucose needs a transport protein to cross a cell surface membrane. Read this answer. Look at the words too large here. It can feel right, since a glucose molecule is bigger than an oxygen molecule, and bigger sounds harder to get through. The June 2023 report on this question says that most incorrect answers gave that reason. The mark scheme credited a different property: glucose is polar, and the core of the bilayer is hydrophobic. At that point it gave nothing for size alone, and nothing for naming facilitated diffusion or active transport. So state the property and the barrier first. In place: glucose is polar, so it does not cross the hydrophobic core of the phospholipid bilayer readily; it needs a transport protein, such as a carrier.
